name: ChronosEngine
problem: Standard system clocks are susceptible to NTP leaps, network skews, and lack reliable monotonicity across distributed processes, making distributed transaction ordering non-deterministic.
pain: Debugging race conditions and causal consistency violations across microservices due to imprecise time synchronization leads to silent data corruption.
solution: A zero-dependency Hybrid Logical Clock (HLC) and event-sequencing engine written in Java 21 that combines physical wall-clock time with logical counters to guarantee causal ordering without heavy coordination.
verification: Deterministic unit tests simulating extreme NTP time jumps, clock drift corrections, and out-of-order message delivery to verify causal consistency invariants and monotonicity.
major_features: Hybrid Logical Clock implementation combining wall-clock millis with logical counters
Causality tracking engine validating happened-before relationships between distributed events
NTP clock drift detector and dynamic skew compensator handling backward time jumps
Lock-free state machine registry updating local timestamps atomically via VarHandles
Binary serialization layout packing timestamps and event payloads into compact byte arrays
Loopback TCP network simulation harness injecting arbitrary network delays and packet reordering
Causal dependency violation detector throwing immediate runtime exceptions on ordering breaches
Comprehensive metrics collector logging physical time deltas and logical counter overflow frequencies
truth_policy: Only validated behavior may be claimed as working.
